result.summary:
I reviewed the Next.js 16.4 and React 19.3 usage at HEAD. First I read the bundled guides for use cache, cacheComponents, partialPrefetching, generateStaticParams/dynamicParams, ensureStatic/instant, notFound/not-found, redirects, outputFileTracing, metadata and next/image. Then I checked the running build on port 3300 and made scratch copies of HEAD in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/build-a and build-b. Those copies were used for a clean `next build` (no warnings), eslint (clean), `next dev` and fix experiments on ports 3311 and 3312, which I stopped afterwards; port 3300 was not touched. The scripts are in the same cr-nextjs folder (crawl.js, nav-ids.js, progress-flow.js, stale-reset.js, nojs.js, hash-nav*.js, dev-check*.js).

These checks passed:
- **Prerendering:** all 79 Lesson pages and 7 Course pages are complete prerenders. In the prerender manifest they are response "complete" and compute "static", and only the [slug] and [course] fallback shells are postponed.
- **File tracing:** every route's .nft.json includes all 87 content/ files.
- **Redirects:** the three old addresses return 308 to the new Slugs and keep query strings.
- **Titles:** every page type has the right "X · Idea to Shipped" title and description, except 404 pages.
- **next/image:** the image optimizer returns 200, and every header image exists in public/.
- **Client/server boundary:** no client chunk contains fs, the content loaders, drizzle, neon, yaml or zod.
- **Hydration:** there are no hydration warnings in production or in dev, with progress empty or stored. useSyncExternalStore server snapshots are stable, and all Date and locale formatting happens after hydration. Option shuffling runs only on the server and is deterministic.
- **Progress:** the its-progress-v1 save and reload works, as do ticks, Course progress, Continue, the /progress page and reset across pages.
- **Duplicate ids:** pages kept hidden by Activity do duplicate ids such as _S_1_ and final-test, but Next always moves the visible route first in the DOM, so aria-labelledby resolves to the right element.
- **Comments:** the API and the Discussion behave as before. Validation errors return 400. With no reachable database the route returns 500 and the Discussion shows "Couldn't load comments."
- **Server log:** it only contains the expected Neon connection errors.

I found 7 defects, listed below.

findings.where: src/app/learn/[slug]/page.tsx:30-32 and src/app/courses/[course]/page.tsx:55-57; http://localhost:3300/learn/<any new slug>, any width
findings.problem: The first request for a Lesson or Course slug that generateStaticParams doesn't list returns HTTP 200, not 404. Since Next 16.3, a param that isn't in the list gets the route's fallback App Shell while the page is built in the background. Here that shell is empty, because both pages await params at the top with no Suspense (.next/server/app/learn/[slug].html is 0 bytes with status 200 and a postponed state). So the 200 is sent before notFound() runs. The body is Next's empty <html id="__next_error__"> shell, so the page is blank without JS and the 404 only appears once JS runs. Repro: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:3300/learn/brand-new-1` returns 200 with x-nextjs-postponed: 1 and Cache-Control: private, no-store. The same URL again returns 404 with x-nextjs-cache: HIT. /courses/brand-new-1 behaves the same way. /learn/nope and /courses/nope only return 404 now because an earlier request already cached them.
findings.fix: Add `export const ensureStatic = "navigation";` to both pages, together with `export const instant = false;` (see F2; with ensureStatic alone, `next dev` logs 'InvariantError: Route "/learn/[slug]" did not produce a static shell' for unknown slugs). I verified this in a scratch build of HEAD. The build passes, and it now also enforces that both routes stay fully static. The first request to /learn/zz-* and /courses/zz-* returns 404, and known pages still return 200. The 404 body is still Next's client-rendered error shell. If a server-rendered 404 matters for visitors without JS, check the slug in proxy.ts and rewrite to the not-found page.

findings.where: src/app/layout.tsx:42 (header "Courses", <Link href="/#courses">) and src/app/page.tsx:59 ("Browse the Courses", <Link href="#courses">); http://localhost:3300/ at 1366px and 390px
findings.problem: next/link mishandles a link to the current page's own hash. (a) Open http://localhost:3300/#courses (or reload after using the Courses link), scroll to the top and click the header's "Courses". Nothing scrolls, and the URL becomes /#courses#courses. (b) Open /, click "Browse the Courses" (it scrolls), scroll back to the top, then click it or the header's "Courses" again. Nothing happens and scrollY stays 0. A plain <a href="#courses"> on the same page scrolls to y=1448. Pressing Enter on the link does the same as a click, so the main nav link stops working for keyboard users too.
findings.fix: Render "Browse the Courses" (and the Course page's "See all the Courses" when it targets the current page) as a plain <a href="#courses">. A jump within the same page doesn't need the router. Make the header link a small client component that keeps <Link href="/#courses"> on other pages. When window.location.pathname is "/", its onClick should call preventDefault, scroll #courses into view (and focus it), and set the hash with history.replaceState.

findings.problem: Three published Slugs were renamed: spec-and-issues to to-spec, pr-and-ship to pr, and architecture to improve-codebase-architecture. The 308s move readers to the new pages, but Comment rows still carry the old lesson_slug, and listComments only queries the new slug. Every Comment already posted on those three Lessons therefore disappears from their Discussion. src/lessons/course.test.ts:36-38 says these Comments 'need moving to the new Slug, or they no longer show', but nothing moves them, and the old slug is now refused. Repro (needs the real database): given a row with lesson_slug='spec-and-issues', GET /api/comments?lesson=to-spec doesn't return it, and GET /api/comments?lesson=spec-and-issues returns 400 "Unknown lesson."
findings.fix: Add a custom migration, for example `drizzle-kit generate --custom --name move-renamed-lesson-comments`, holding `UPDATE comments SET lesson_slug='to-spec' WHERE lesson_slug='spec-and-issues';` and the same for 'pr' and 'improve-codebase-architecture'. `npm run build` already runs drizzle-kit migrate before next build. Alternatively, have listComments also read the old slugs from RENAMED_LESSONS.

findings.where: src/app/learn/[slug]/page.tsx:31 and src/app/courses/[course]/page.tsx:56 (next dev, every Course and Lesson URL)
findings.problem: Under `next dev`, every Course and Lesson page logs an error to the terminal, the browser console and the dev overlay: 'Route "/learn/[slug]": Next.js encountered URL data during prerendering or a navigation. `params` ... accessed outside of <Suspense> may prevent the navigation from being instant'. This is Instant Navigation validation, which cacheComponents turns on by default. An unknown slug also logs 'Could not validate `instant` because an error prevented the target segment from rendering.' Repro: run next dev on a copy and open /learn/what-git-and-github-are or /courses/ci-cd; the console error points at page.tsx:31 or :56. Production logs are clean, but the cause is real there too. With partialPrefetching, the App Shell a default <Link> prefetches holds none of these pages, so every Course or Lesson click waits for a server round trip with no loading UI.
findings.fix: Add `export const instant = false;` to both pages. This is the documented [block] option, and these routes are fully prerendered, so blocking on their static payload is the intended behaviour. I verified that it removes both dev errors, including when combined with ensureStatic from F1. If navigations should be instant instead, give Lesson and Course links prefetch={true}.

findings.problem: flashcards.tsx is a Client Component, and it imports htmlToText from @/lessons/markdown. That module imports marked and runs `new Marked({...})` at load time, so the whole Markdown parser ships to every Lesson page. In the build, the Lesson-only chunk .next/static/chunks/0lfsx4pfho1n_.js is 64 KB, and about 56 KB of it is marked (about 17 KB gzipped): it contains 'Please report this to https://github.com/markedjs/marked' and the ==mark== extension. route-bundle-stats.json shows 553 KB first-load JS for /learn/[slug] against 488 KB for the other routes. The browser only needs a 3-line regex.
findings.fix: Move htmlToText and its ENTITIES map into a module with no imports (for example src/lessons/html-text.ts). Import it from flashcards.tsx and re-export it from markdown.ts. Alternatively, send each card's plain-text front and back from the server.

findings.problem: With cacheComponents, Next keeps visited routes mounted in <Activity>. FinalTest's local `result` state therefore survives navigation, and nothing checks it against the progress store. Repro: on /learn/what-git-and-github-are, answer all 8 questions and submit. Click the header's "Progress", then "Reset my progress" and "Yes, reset my progress", then press Back. its-progress-v1 is gone from localStorage and the header's Done pill has disappeared. The Final test still shows the green 'Done · You got 0 of 8 · This Lesson is marked Done in this browser' banner and the bar 'You got 0 of 8. This Lesson is Done.', with every question still locked.
findings.fix: Tie the shown result to the store. Call progressStore.markDone inside the same flushSync as setResult, and render everything that depends on the result from `const shown = done ? result : null`. A reset on /progress or in another tab then returns the test to its fresh state. Alternatively, clear result and answers when `done` changes from set to null.

findings.where: src/app has no not-found.tsx; src/app/learn/[slug]/page.tsx:20, src/app/courses/[course]/page.tsx:24; http://localhost:3300/learn/nope and /nope
findings.problem: 404 pages ignore the site's title template. In production the title is Next's default '404: This page could not be found.', without '· Idea to Shipped'. The { title: "Not found" } that both generateMetadata functions return is never shown. The server HTML for /learn/nope and /courses/nope has no <title> at all, and /nope sends two (<title>404: This page could not be found.</title> and <title>Idea to Shipped</title>).
findings.fix: Add src/app/not-found.tsx that exports `metadata = { title: "Not found" }` and renders a page in the site's style. I verified this in a scratch build: /nope's HTML gets one <title>Not found · Idea to Shipped</title>, and /learn/<unknown> shows the same title once rendered.

result.evidence:
I reproduced it on the running build at http://localhost:3300 and traced the cause in Next's own code. A patched scratch build fixed it. 1. Repro with curl, using slugs no one had requested before. - The first GET to /learn/cr-fresh- returned HTTP 200 with `x-nextjs-postponed: 1` and `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. - The second request returned 404 (`x-nextjs-cache: MISS`) and the third 404 (HIT). The finding says the second request is the HIT, a trivial difference. - /courses/ behaves the same way. /learn/nope and /courses/nope now return 404 because they are already cached. 2. The 200 body has no visible content. - It is `` with ``. Outside its scripts the body is only `
`. - `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` appears only in the RSC data inside scripts. 3. Repro in Chromium (Playwright). - With JS on, the first visit returns 200 and the 404 UI appears only after JS runs. - With JS off, the page is blank (screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/shot-js-off-fresh-lesson.png). - A URL that matches no route (/_not-found) returns a server-rendered 404 with header and footer. - By user agent: Googlebot and Chrome get 200 on the first hit. Twitterbot gets 404, because the runtime forces a blocking render for HTML-limited bots. 4. Build output matches the finding. - wt-build/.next/server/app/learn/[slug].html and courses/[course].html are 0 bytes. - Their .meta files have "status": 200 and a "postponed" state. 5. Cause in Next's code. - next.config.ts sets `cacheComponents: true` and `partialPrefetching: true`. Partial Prefetching was introduced in 16.3.0, as the finding says. - node_modules/next/dist/build/templates/app-page-runtime.js lines 734-743 switch the fallback mode to `FallbackMode.PRERENDER` when `nextConfig.partialPrefetching && prerenderInfo.fallback === null && !isEnsureStaticPage`. That serves the fallback shell, then resumes the render. - build/static-paths/app.js line 713 sets `BLOCKING_STATIC_RENDER` only for ensureStatic pages. - Both pages await params at the top with no Suspense boundary, so the shell is empty and the 200 goes out before notFound() runs. The 'not-found' doc says a 404 that streams keeps status 200. - The bundled guide incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components.md (line 211) and ensureStatic.md (lines 101-103) say `ensureStatic = 'navigation'` makes the first request for an unlisted param wait for the complete static page. - `dynamicParams` is not available with Cache Components. `unstable_paramMatching` exists but is unstable and undocumented. 6. The fix, verified in a private copy of wt-build at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/f1-verify/fix (port 3317, since stopped). - `next build` passes (log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/f1-verify/build-fix.log). The only manifest change is `_isEnsureStaticPage: true`. - The first request to /learn/zz-* and /courses/zz-* returns 404 (MISS, then HIT). The RSC request for an unknown slug also returns 404; before the fix it returned 200. - Known pages still return 200 from the cache. Their text and h1 match the original build, with JS on and off. - The 308 redirect for renamed slugs still works. Client-side navigation from a Course page to a Lesson does no full page load. - The only console error is a 500 from /api/comments (no database here). The original build shows it too. 7. The `instant = false` claim, checked with `next dev` on another copy (log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/f1-verify/dev.log). - With `ensureStatic` alone, unknown slugs log `InvariantError: Invariant: Route "/learn/[slug]" did not produce a static shell ... This is a bug in Next.js`, and the same for /courses/[course]. - With `instant = false` added, those errors are gone. - HEAD itself, in dev, logs "Could not validate `instant` because an error prevented the target segment from rendering". Dev always returns 404, so the bug only happens in production. Context: .scratch/lesson-site/issues/03-lesson-pages.md:12 had accepted the 200 for v1 and said a fix needed a Proxy check. No published Lesson relies on the bug: the Try it in content/on-ramps/diagnosing-bugs.md uses the practice project. Limit that remains after the fix: the 404 body is still Next's `__next_error__` shell, so visitors without JS see a blank page. This was already true of the cached 404 before the fix.

Confirmed, both from the code and by reproduction.

The code:
- src/comments/comments.ts:60-66: `listComments` first calls `isLesson(lesson)`. That calls `courses.lessonExists`, which is just `lessons.has(slug)` (src/lessons/lessons.ts:318-319) and knows no old slugs. It then queries only `.where(eq(comments.lessonSlug, lesson))`. Only next.config.ts (for the `/learn/:old` redirects) and course.test.ts read `RENAMED_LESSONS`.
- src/app/learn/[slug]/page.tsx:71 renders `<Discussion slug={lesson.slug} />`, and discussion.tsx:16 fetches `/api/comments?lesson=<slug>`. After the 308, that slug is the new one.
- drizzle/ holds only 0000_create_comments.sql, with one journal entry. `git log --all -- drizzle/` shows only c413630, and no branch or `.claude/worktrees` copy has a second migration. No code anywhere updates `lesson_slug`.
- course.test.ts:36-38 itself says the old-slug Comments "need moving to the new Slug, or they no longer show". ADR 0004 says a published slug never changes.
- Production can hold such rows. origin/main (fae17a9) serves content/idea-to-shipped/spec-and-issues.md, pr-and-ship.md and architecture.md, with matching `slug:` headers. Each page has a Discussion, and there are no redirects.

The live build at http://localhost:3300:
- `GET /api/comments?lesson=` with spec-and-issues, pr-and-ship or architecture returns 400 `{"error":"Unknown lesson."}`.
- `/learn/<old>` returns 308 to the new slug.
- GETs for the new slugs return 500 there, but only because that server's DATABASE_URL is a dummy (the server log shows "fetch failed"). So I ran the database half separately.

Real-SQL repro: Node 24 ran the repo's unchanged route.ts, comments.ts, lessons.ts and schema.ts. Only `@/db` was swapped for drizzle-orm/pglite (PGlite is Postgres compiled to WebAssembly). The schema came from the repo's committed drizzle/ folder, applied with drizzle's migrator. I added one row under each old slug, then posted one Comment to to-spec through the real POST handler.
- `GET ?lesson=to-spec` returns 200 `["posted on /learn/to-spec after the rename"]`. The spec-and-issues row is missing.
- `?lesson=pr` and `?lesson=improve-codebase-architecture` each return 200 `[]`.
- Each old slug returns 400 "Unknown lesson."
- The table still holds one row each under architecture, pr-and-ship and spec-and-issues.

Fix check:
- `drizzle-kit generate --custom --name move-renamed-lesson-comments` (drizzle-kit 0.31.11, run in a scratch copy, no database needed) writes drizzle/0001_move-renamed-lesson-comments.sql, drizzle/meta/0001_snapshot.json and a second journal entry.
- I filled it with the UPDATEs below and simulated a deploy: a database with 0000 applied and old-slug rows, then migrated with 0000+0001.
- Only 0001 ran (two migrations recorded). GET to-spec then returned `["new Comment on /learn/to-spec","old Comment from /learn/spec-and-issues"]`, and pr and improve-codebase-architecture each showed their old Comment.
- Running migrate again ran nothing.
- The read-side alternative also passed the same harness: all three old Comments show, and no rows move.

result.fix:
1. In /home/user/idea-to-shipped, run `npm run db:generate -- --custom --name move-renamed-lesson-comments` (that is, `drizzle-kit generate --custom --name move-renamed-lesson-comments`; it needs no database). Commit the three files it writes: drizzle/0001_move-renamed-lesson-comments.sql, drizzle/meta/0001_snapshot.json, and the new idx 1 entry in drizzle/meta/_journal.json.

2. In drizzle/0001_move-renamed-lesson-comments.sql, under the generated header line `-- Custom SQL migration file, put your code below! --`, put:
UPDATE "comments" SET "lesson_slug" = 'to-spec' WHERE "lesson_slug" = 'spec-and-issues';
--> statement-breakpoint
UPDATE "comments" SET "lesson_slug" = 'pr' WHERE "lesson_slug" = 'pr-and-ship';
--> statement-breakpoint
UPDATE "comments" SET "lesson_slug" = 'improve-codebase-architecture' WHERE "lesson_slug" = 'architecture';
Keep the breakpoint lines, as drizzle-kit's own 0000 file does. drizzle's migrator runs each chunk as one query, all inside one transaction. This exact file is the one I tested.

3. Nothing else is needed for deploys. `npm run build` already runs `drizzle-kit migrate` before `next build`, so each Vercel deploy applies the migration once, on its own Neon branch. Locally, run `npm run db:migrate` and `npm run db:migrate:test`.

4. Optional: change the comment at src/lessons/course.test.ts:36-38 (and the GLOSSARY "Slug" entry) to say the Comments were moved by drizzle/0001_move-renamed-lesson-comments.sql, and that any future rename needs a migration of its own.

Caveat, and an alternative that avoids it: the migration runs at the start of the production build, while the old deployment is still serving. Until the new deployment is live, the old /learn/<old> pages show empty Discussions, and a Comment posted there in that window keeps the old slug and stays hidden. If `next build` fails after migrating, that lasts until the next successful deploy.

Changing the read side instead has no such window. In src/comments/comments.ts:
- replace `import { desc, eq } from "drizzle-orm";` with `import { desc, inArray } from "drizzle-orm";`
- add `import { RENAMED_LESSONS } from "../../next.config";` (course.test.ts already imports it this way; keep the map in next.config.ts, because the Next 16 docs limit module resolution in that file)
- add `const formerSlugs = (lesson: string) => Object.keys(RENAMED_LESSONS).filter((old) => RENAMED_LESSONS[old] === lesson);`
- in `listComments`, change `.where(eq(comments.lessonSlug, lesson))` to `.where(inArray(comments.lessonSlug, [lesson, ...formerSlugs(lesson)]))`

I checked that change with the same harness but did not run it through `next build`. If you choose it, add a database test to src/app/api/comments/route.test.ts: insert `{ lessonSlug: "spec-and-issues", body: "old" }` with `db.insert(comments)`, then check that `GET ?lesson=to-spec` includes "old".

result.evidence:
Reproduced on http://localhost:3300 with Playwright at 1366x768 and 390x844, using my own scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/ (f6-repro.js, f6-verify.js, f6-fixcheck.js, f6-crosspage.js).

(a) Load /#courses, scrollTo(0,0), click the header "Courses": scrollY stays 0 and the router pushes /#courses#courses (history.length goes up by 1).

(b) Load / and click "Browse the Courses": it scrolls to y=1294 at 1366px (2013 at 390px). Scroll back to the top. A second click on Browse, a click on the header "Courses", and Enter on the header link all leave scrollY at 0. Tab after Enter lands on "Progress". A plain <a href="#courses"> injected as a control scrolls every time.

Root cause, in next 16.4.3 (node_modules/next/dist/client/components):
- No scroll: app-router-state.js:362-364 sets onlyHashChange only when url.hash !== oldUrl.hash. Repeating the current hash takes the default branch (line 421) with no new segments and no scrollRef, so layout-router.js:104-105 returns without scrolling. That contradicts the Link docs (link.md:894): "When there is a hash defined it will scroll to the specific id, like a normal <a> tag".
- Doubled hash: router-reducer/create-initial-router-state.js:28-30 and 62 store createHrefFromUrl(location), hash included, as the route cache entry's canonicalUrl. app-router-state.js:204 then builds route.canonicalUrl + url.hash. The unknown-route path (lines 282-284) deliberately stores a hashless URL.

The proposed fix has two flaws, both reproduced:
1. A plain <a href="#courses"> makes a native fragment navigation, whose history entry has null state, and app-router.js:62-65 (handlePopState) ignores null state. Flow: plain anchor, then a Course card, then Back. The URL becomes /#courses, but the Course page stays on screen (h1 "GitHub from zero"). With the current next/link, the same flow restores the home page.
2. Keeping <Link href="/#courses"> on other pages still doubles the hash. Start the session at /#courses, open a Course card, then click "See all the Courses" or the header "Courses": the URL is /#courses#courses in 4 of 4 runs on 3300. The Course page's button never targets the current page, so the "when it targets the current page" case never arises.

Two smaller problems: onClick also runs on Ctrl/Cmd-click (link.js:297-309), so it would need its own modifier-key check. And "focus it" does nothing without tabIndex={-1} on the target.

The fix below was tested in a patched copy (cr-nextjs/f6-build): `next build` passed, including its TypeScript step, and ESLint was clean. Served on :3461 and checked with f6-verify.js, at both widths:
- every click and every Enter scrolls (1294 / 2013), and the URL stays /#courses
- focus moves to #courses-title, and the next Tab reaches the first Course card
- Browse, then a Course card, then Back restores the home page (history.state keeps __NA)
- Ctrl+click opens /#courses in a new tab and leaves the current tab where it is
- restore-reducer leaves state.scrollRef unchanged (app-router-state.js:471), so the restore that pushState fires causes no stray scroll

One difference showed up: my test build scrolled before calling pushState, so Back from /#courses to / stayed at y=1294, where the original returns to y=0. The browser saves the old entry's scroll position when pushState runs. The fix below therefore calls pushState first. I reasoned that change but did not rebuild to re-check it, because plan mode started.

Not fixed by either version: the cross-page /#courses#courses. It didn't show on the fresh :3461 build because build-time HTML carries InliningHintsStale. segment-cache/cache.js:975-976 then sets staleAt=-1, so the home page's Link prefetch fetched /_tree and wrote a hashless entry (seen in the request log). On 3300, whose page has revalidated (revalidate 15m), no prefetch happens, and the hash-bearing entry stays in use for up to the 5-minute static stale time.

Housekeeping: my scratch server on :3461 is still running. Its PID is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/f6-server.pid. Stop it with `kill $(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-nextjs/f6-server.pid)`; I left it up because plan mode started.
